summary_paragraph: A 54-year-old woman with idiopathic chronic pancreatitis was admitted for an acute flare characterized by worsening epigastric pain and vomiting. Imaging showed no pancreatic abnormalities, and she was managed with bowel rest, TPN, IV fluids, and pain control, including a fentanyl patch for improved analgesia. During her hospitalization, she developed a nosocomial pneumonia, evidenced by fever and progressive right lung opacity on chest imaging, and was treated with antibiotics. She was found to have anemia due to iron deficiency and chronic inflammation, confirmed by low ferritin and transferrin, and underwent EGD which showed chronic inactive gastritis with intestinal metaplasia but no bleeding. She received one unit of PRBCs for a hematocrit of 23.9% and was advised to complete a colonoscopy as an outpatient. Pancytopenia and eosinophilia were noted but deemed stable and chronic. She improved clinically, tolerated a clear diet, and was discharged home with visiting nurse support for TPN and line care, a 7-day antibiotic course, and close outpatient follow-up.
